passkeyGuide.title: Passkeys
passkeyGuide.intro: Passkeys let admins sign in with Touch ID, Windows Hello, or a security key instead of a password. The two settings below tie a passkey to this exact site — get them wrong and passkeys will fail to register or sign in.
passkeyGuide.rpIdBody: The domain the dashboard is served from, without a protocol or port — for example example.com.

telegramGuide.title: Telegram OAuth2
telegramGuide.intro: Setting up “Sign in with Telegram” requires a Telegram bot, and that bot needs some extra configuration for the feature to work correctly.
botSetupSteps: Open the Mini App via the “Open” button
Select your bot and open Login Widget
If a domain is already set in the URL field, remove it
Press Switch to OpenID Connect Login. If that button isn’t there, go back a menu after removing the domain and repeat step 3
Press Add a Redirect URI and Add a Trusted Origin and enter the values below:
telegramGuide.accessSetupIntro: After filling in the Client ID and Client secret, you need to list the admin IDs allowed to sign in.
accessSetupSteps: From the account you want to grant access, message @Get_myidrobot
The bot replies with your ID — enter it into the corresponding field
telegramGuide.knownIssuesIntro: Protections layered in front of the dashboard (cookie policies and similar) can misbehave with Telegram OAuth2.
telegramGuide.knownIssuesProxyTip: Use the /oauth2/ path in your reverse proxy to work around this.
telegramGuide.errorBotDomainBody: This happens when the bot’s domain isn’t configured correctly — revisit “Setting up the bot” above and redo it step by step if needed.
telegramGuide.errorNoCodeTitle: Error: no confirmation code arrives from Telegram at login
telegramGuide.errorNoCodeBody: This isn’t something fixable on Remnashop’s side. Try a bot created a while ago, or a different browser. You can also try signing in on one of Telegram’s own “official” surfaces first, e.g. fragment.com — since the Telegram session is shared within the browser, that can help the panel sign-in go through.

githubGuide.title: OAuth2: GitHub
githubGuide.createAppIntro: First, create an OAuth app. Follow this link to create one:
githubGuide.callbackIntro: Under Authorization callback URL, enter your dashboard’s address.
githubGuide.callbackCommentLabel: Replace YOUR_REMNASHOP_DOMAIN with your dashboard’s address
githubGuide.callbackNote: Don’t forget to replace YOUR_REMNASHOP_DOMAIN with your dashboard’s actual address.
githubGuide.settingsBody: Once the OAuth app is created, copy the Client ID and Client secret. Paste them into the corresponding fields.

oidcGuide.title: OpenID Connect (SSO)
oidcGuide.intro: Any OIDC-compliant provider works — Keycloak, Authentik, Zitadel, Auth0, PocketID, and others. The issuer must serve the standard /.well-known/openid-configuration endpoint.

sections.title: What it does
sections.body: Before an email code is sent, the customer passes a check from the chosen provider. This keeps bots from sending codes to other people’s addresses and getting your SMTP into spam lists. Telegram and OAuth sign-in are not affected.

sections.title: Cloudflare Turnstile
sections.body: In the Cloudflare dashboard open Turnstile, add a widget with the cabinet domain and copy its site key and secret key.

sections.title: hCaptcha
sections.body: In the hCaptcha dashboard add a site with the cabinet domain, copy its site key and the account secret key.

sections.title: If the provider is down
sections.body: Email codes are not sent while the provider can’t confirm the check; the other sign-in methods keep working.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: On the sign-in page the customer presses the Telegram button: the bot opens and sends a confirmation button that signs them in to the cabinet. When the cabinet is opened as a Mini App inside Telegram, sign-in happens automatically.

sections.title: Requirements
sections.body: A bot token in the “Telegram bot” section and the cabinet domain in the CABINET_DOMAIN environment variable.

sections.title: Mini App
sections.body: Optional. To open the cabinet right from Telegram, in @BotFather pick the bot → Mini Apps, enable the Main App and set the cabinet address. The same address can go into the Menu Button so the cabinet also opens from the menu button in the bot chat.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: A Telegram OAuth button appears on the sign-in page. The client ID and secret are shared with Telegram in “OAuth providers”: changing them here changes them for dashboard sign-in too.

sections.title: Bot setup
sections.body: If Telegram OAuth isn’t set up yet, follow the “Telegram OAuth2” guide in “OAuth providers”. Then in @BotFather pick the bot → Login Widget and add the cabinet addresses next to the dashboard ones: Add a Redirect URI and Add a Trusted Origin.

sections.title: Creating a client
sections.body: Open the Clients page in Google Cloud Console, press Create Client and pick the Web application type. If OAuth isn’t set up in the project yet, the console asks you to fill in the consent screen first.

sections.title: Redirect URI
sections.body: Add the address below to Authorized redirect URIs, replacing YOUR_CABINET_DOMAIN with the cabinet domain:

sections.title: Keys
sections.body: Copy the Client ID and Client secret into the fields below. The cabinet only requests the name and email address (openid, email, profile).

sections.title: Creating an app
sections.body: Create an app “For user authorization” and pick the “Web services” platform.

sections.title: Redirect URI
sections.body: Set the Redirect URI to the address below, replacing YOUR_CABINET_DOMAIN with the cabinet domain:

sections.title: Data access and keys
sections.body: Under data access pick “Login, first and last name, gender” and “Email address”. After saving, copy the ClientID and Client secret from the app page into the fields below.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The customer enters an email address, receives a one-time code and enters it on the sign-in page.

sections.title: Requirements
sections.body: SMTP configured in the “SMTP” card below; without it the method can’t be enabled.

sections.title: Domain restriction
sections.body: To keep out disposable mailboxes, enable “Only allowed email domains”: new email sign-ups are accepted only from domains on the list.

u.primary: Main actions, dialog and form footers. 14px.

u.period: Period picker: transactions, ads, dashboard, analytics.
u.pillTabs: Dialog editor, backups, translations; field — 38px beside a search.
u.choice: One of a small set; sm — dense grids.
u.badge: Status: uppercase with a border, colored by tone.
u.tag: Counts and metadata: gray pill, no uppercase.

u.cardForm: Form section in a dialog, 11px title.
u.cardList: InfoRow rows, title with an icon.
u.kpiIcon: With an icon and a label hint.

u.fieldHint: Hint icon by a label: up, down, at the right edge.

u.cardHeader: Page and settings card header: icon, title, description, right-side block, divider

kpi.failedHint: Can be retried once sending ends

channel.title: Channel post
channel.planned: Will be published in the channel
channel.recallHint: Recalling deletes the post along with the private messages.

cancel.title: Stop the broadcast?
cancel.message: Messages that haven’t been sent yet won’t go out. Delivered ones stay.

retry.unavailable: Nothing to retry: no failed deliveries.
retry.title: Retry failed deliveries?
retry.message: Customers with errors will get the message again. Those who blocked the bot are skipped.

recall.unavailable: Messages can be recalled within 48 hours of the start, if something was delivered.
recall.running: The recall is running. You can repeat it in a few minutes if some messages remain.
recall.title: Recall the broadcast?
recall.message: Delivered messages are deleted from customers’ chats and the channel post is removed. This can’t be undone.

delete.title: Delete the broadcast?
delete.message: The broadcast and its delivery history will be deleted. This can’t be undone.
